_source: https://github.com/Halluminate/WebBench (webbenchfinal.csv), fetched 2026-08-17 via the GitHub contents API (raw.githubusercontent.com returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests for this repo at run time; the API endpoint returns the identical 818,409-byte file, base64-encoded)
_note: Tenth Claude-direct sample, and the FIRST one driven by Opus rather than Sonnet. Samples 1-9 were all Sonnet-driven; the user asked to isolate host-model quality as an explicit variable — same tool (Sutradhar's real CLI binary), same methodology, same honest scoring standard, different brain — to see whether a stronger host model changes the real completion rate (better workaround reasoning on ambiguous/drifted tasks, less likely to give up early). 10 fresh READ-category domains, none previously attempted (checked against tools/webbench/tested-domains.txt). Deliberately NOT cherry-picked for easiness: the spread spans retail, dictionary, gov/science, national-parks, gaming media, dev Q&A, film, education, a utility site, and a reference site — including domains with known heavy anti-bot posture. IDs match the dataset's own row IDs.
